theory.intro: An **arithmetic sequence** (or **arithmetic progression**) has a constant **common difference** $d$ between consecutive terms. Each term is obtained by adding $d$ to the previous term.
facts: The common difference is $d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}$ for any term index $n \ge 2$.
The $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is $a_{n} = a + (n - 1)d$, where $a$ is the first term.
If $d > 0$ the sequence increases, if $d < 0$ it decreases, and if $d = 0$ it is constant.
The term $a_{n}$ is a linear function of $n$ with gradient $d$ restricted to positive integer inputs.

workedExamples.question_text:
For each sequence, test whether it is an AP. If it is, state $a$ and $d$.
(a) $6,13,20,27,\ldots$
(b) $42,34,26,18,\ldots$
(c) $5,14,24,\ldots$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $13-6=7$, $20-13=7$ and $27-20=7$.
The difference is constant, so $a=6$ and $d=7$.
(b) $34-42=-8$, $26-34=-8$ and $18-26=-8$.
The difference is constant, so $a=42$ and $d=-8$.
(c) $14-5=9$ but $24-14=10$.
The differences are not equal, so this is not an AP.

workedExamples.question_text:
An arithmetic sequence has first term $a=-17$ and common difference $d=4.5$.
(a) Find a simplified formula for $a_n$.
(b) Find $a_{16}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{aligned}a_n&=a+(n-1)d\\a_n&=-17+4.5(n-1)\\a_n&=-17+4.5n-4.5\\a_n&=4.5n-21.5\end{aligned}$
The coefficient of $n$ is $4.5$: increasing $n$ by $1$ increases the term by $4.5$.
(b)
$\begin{aligned}a_{16}&=4.5(16)-21.5\\a_{16}&=72-21.5\\a_{16}&=50.5\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: How many terms are in the finite AP $62,55,48,\ldots,-71$?
Find the position and value of the first negative term in the AP $82,76,70,\ldots$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$a=82$, $d=-6$.
$\begin{aligned}a_n&=82+(n-1)(-6)\\a_n&=88-6n\end{aligned}$
For a negative term, $a_n<0$.
$\begin{aligned}88-6n&<0\\6n&>88\\n&>\frac{44}{3}\end{aligned}$
The first integer position is $n=15$.
$a_{15}=88-6(15)=-2$.
The preceding term is $a_{14}=88-6(14)=4$, so the first negative term is $-2$, at position $15$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) An AP has $a_4=29$ and $a_{11}=78$. Find $a$, $d$ and $a_{18}$.
(b) Another AP has $a_2+a_6=43$ and $a_9=38$. Find $a$ and $d$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $a+3d=29\quad\text{(1)}$
$a+10d=78\quad\text{(2)}$
Subtract (1) from (2).
$\begin{aligned}7d&=49\\d&=7\end{aligned}$
Substitute into (1).
$\begin{aligned}a+3(7)&=29\\a&=8\end{aligned}$
$a_{18}=8+17(7)=127$.
(b) $(a+d)+(a+5d)=43$, so $2a+6d=43\quad\text{(1)}$.
$a+8d=38$, so $2a+16d=76\quad\text{(2)}$.
Subtract (1) from (2).
$\begin{aligned}10d&=33\\d&=3.3\end{aligned}$
Substitute into $a+8d=38$.
$\begin{aligned}a+8(3.3)&=38\\a+26.4&=38\\a&=11.6\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: For what value of $x$ is $3x-7,5x+4,8x-9$ an AP? Find its $10$th term.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The consecutive differences must be equal.
$\begin{aligned}(5x+4)-(3x-7)&=(8x-9)-(5x+4)\\2x+11&=3x-13\\x&=24\end{aligned}$
The terms are $65,124,183$, so $a=65$ and $d=59$.
$\begin{aligned}a_{10}&=65+(10-1)(59)\\a_{10}&=65+531\\a_{10}&=596\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text: Determine whether the sequence $4, 11, 18, 25, \dots$ is an arithmetic progression, and if so, state the first term $a$ and common difference $d$.
foundation.solution_text:
$a_2 - a_1 = 11 - 4 = 7$
$a_3 - a_2 = 18 - 11 = 7$
$\text{The difference is constant, so it is an AP with } a = 4 \text{ and } d = 7.$
